comparator.name: Linguistics
comparator.sourceNotes: The current official UvA programme page reconstructs a complete 180-EC Linguistics bachelor. Year 1 contains ten 6-EC components: Introduction to Linguistics, four 6-EC Language X restricted-choice components, Phonetics, Transcription, Morphology, Sociolinguistics and a first-year research project. Year 2 contains ten named 6-EC compulsory components spanning acquisition, philosophy, phonology, psycholinguistics, syntax, clinical linguistics, neurolinguistics, semantics/pragmatics and linguistic theory. Year 3 contains Speech Processing, Research Methods & Statistics and a Linguistics specialisation at 6 EC each, 30 EC of genuine free choice and a 12-EC bachelor thesis. Published restricted and free-choice space is preserved generically without inventing course titles.

exception.reason: The UvA bachelor requires a 60-EC first-year foundation in linguistic structure, phonetics, transcription, morphology, sociolinguistics, modern-language study and linguistic research; a further 60 EC of compulsory acquisition, phonology, syntax, semantics/pragmatics, psycholinguistics, neurolinguistics and clinical linguistics; and advanced speech processing, specialisation and an independent Linguistics thesis. Even allowing the genuine 30-EC free-choice space, UCR has no coherent foundational sequence in phonetics, phonology, morphology, syntax, semantic theory, sociolinguistics, language acquisition, clinical linguistics or speech processing. A 24-course response built mainly from communication, psychology, cognition and data science would replace the discipline with neighbouring fields.
exception.curriculumContext: The live UvA curriculum totals exactly 180 EC: 60 EC in ten first-year units, 60 EC in ten second-year units, and a third year comprising three named 6-EC units, 30 EC of genuine free choice and a 12-EC bachelor thesis. The four Language X units are formal restricted-choice curriculum components and are retained without selecting a language for UCR convenience.
exception.ucrCourseEvidence: Reviewed the current enriched UCR workbook covering all 151 course rows, including descriptions, outline-derived profiles, topics, prerequisites and planned terms. HCBCOGN312 Psycholinguistics studies acquisition, processing and neurocognitive language factors; MCCCOMM211 Style & Meaning considers linguistic choices in texts; MCCCOMM111, MCCCOMM213 and MCCCOMM311 address rhetoric, discourse and persuasion; MCCCOMM112 teaches introductory Dutch; and HCBCOGN311 includes language among higher cognitive functions. BENGATE102 and HCBPSYC211 provide research and statistics, while DISDATA311 and related computing courses touch language models or data analysis. These are discrete neighbouring perspectives. The workbook has no stand-alone phonetics, phonology, morphology, syntax, semantics, sociolinguistics, language-acquisition, clinical-linguistics or speech-processing progression and therefore cannot support a credible complete Linguistics programme.
